m1-fixnow-artifact-ref.title: Fix-now: artifact-ref entries are not stripped before storage
m1-fixnow-artifact-ref.imperative: The g2 review's carried defect: _apply_create() strips every other agent-facing string but stores artifact-ref verbatim, while parse_episode() strips the whole line before FIELD_RE matching — so an artifact-ref with trailing whitespace writes, then silently loses that whitespace on the next parse (render(parse(text)) != text). TDD RED FIRST: add a round-trip test to tests/test_episode_store.py creating an episode whose artifact-ref carries trailing whitespace, asserting render(parse(text)) == text and that the stored line has no trailing space; observe it fail. Then make the ONE-LINE fix in scripts/apply_episode_delta.py (_apply_create: strip each artifact-ref, exactly as every sibling mechanical field is stripped). Touch nothing else in that file.

postconditions.satisfied_by: RED observed: stored line was '- artifact-ref: docs/EPISODE_STORE.md   ' (trailing spaces), assertion failed before the fix

postconditions.statement: green: the round-trip test passes and the whole existing writer suite still passes

m2-fetch-enumerate.imperative: Create scripts/query_episodes.py. Fetch by id calls resolve_episode_path() (never constructs a path); enumerate-all calls iter_episode_ids() (never globs). Both parse via parse_episode(). Read files with encoding='utf-8', newline='' like the writer. TDD red first.

m3-select.title: Select by exact field value / set membership + the silent-omission adversarial fixture
m3-select.imperative: Add select(): enumerate, then match EXACTLY — line-anchored, no substring matching — on a mechanical field, with set-membership semantics (a value set; artifact-ref is list-valued so it matches on non-empty intersection). An unrecognized field name must FAIL VISIBLY, never return an empty candidate set. Adversarial fixture (headline anti-silent-omission evidence): an episode whose match is on a NON-FINAL artifact-ref among several. A naive implementation that folds mechanical '- key: value' lines into a dict keeps only the LAST artifact-ref and silently returns one record short — no error, no crash. The test must run the naive implementation and ours over the same fixture and assert naive omits while ours returns the complete set. Pair a second adversarial case: a substring-matching naive select over values where one is a prefix of another. TDD red first.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: select + adversarial silent-omission tests written and observed failing — manual attest
postconditions.satisfied_by: RED observed: 9 failed (select/field_values absent) before implementation

postconditions.statement: green: select is exact/line-anchored, unknown field fails visibly, and the naive-vs-ours omission comparison passes

constraints: exact match and set membership only — no ranking, scoring, similarity

m4-neighbours.title: Neighbour enumeration by shared exact join key + its own omission fixture
m4-neighbours.imperative: Add neighbours(): for episode E, every OTHER episode sharing at least one exact join key with E. Join keys (my decision, logged): (1) any shared artifact-ref value; (2) the (role, spine-step) pair. The result is the UNION over all join keys — complete by construction, unranked, self excluded. Adversarial fixture: E has one artifact-ref neighbour and one distinct (role, spine-step) neighbour; a naive implementation that returns on the first matching join key silently omits the other. Run naive vs ours over the same store and assert the omission. TDD red first.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: neighbour tests + join-key omission fixture written and observed failing — manual attest
postconditions.satisfied_by: RED observed: 6 failed (neighbour_ids absent) before implementation

postconditions.statement: green: neighbours returns the complete union across join keys; naive first-key-wins version demonstrably omits

constraints: union, never a ranked or truncated set

m5-c2-cross-session.title: C2 — cross-session retrieval across a REAL process boundary
m5-c2-cross-session.imperative: The issue's headline acceptance criterion. Seed an episode by launching scripts/apply_episode_delta.py in one subprocess (sys.executable), then retrieve it by launching scripts/query_episodes.py in a SECOND, separately launched subprocess sharing only the working tree. Prove the boundary is real, not simulated: use subprocess.Popen so each child's OS pid is observed by the parent, have the query child report its own os.getpid() in its JSON envelope, and assert seed_pid != query_pid != the pytest process's own pid. No in-process double call, no shared module state, no warm cache — assert the retrieved record's content equals what was seeded.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: the cross-session test written and observed failing before the retrieval CLI supports it — manual attest
postconditions.satisfied_by: No honest RED available: the retrieval CLI this exercises was already green at m2, so a failing-first version would have had to be manufactured. Substituted a real falsification instead, and BAKED IT IN as test_the_cross_session_exercise_is_not_vacuous: point an identical session 2 at a different empty store root -> rc 2 'no such episode'. The exercise therefore depends on the store on disk and nothing ambient.

postconditions.statement: green: a genuinely fresh interpreter retrieves the seeded episode; three distinct pids asserted

constraints: subprocess + sys.executable; the pid assertion is the proof the boundary is real

m6-c3-cross-worktree.title: C3 — cross-worktree sharing demonstrated through git itself
m6-c3-cross-worktree.imperative: Build a real temp git repo (git init, LOCAL user.email/user.name and commit.gpgsign=false so commit cannot fail on identity or signing), commit an episodes/ directory, then real `git worktree add` TWO linked worktrees. Assert the episode is ABSENT from the reader worktree first (query returns empty there), then seed AND COMMIT it in the writer worktree, merge to main, merge main into the reader worktree — the ordinary git path of EPISODE_STORE.md section 9 — and retrieve it from the reader worktree in a fresh subprocess. Do NOT simulate a worktree with a directory name: paste `git worktree list` as evidence. Windows cleanup must be robust (onerror handler that chmods and retries; read-only .git files resist shutil.rmtree). If this cannot be made real, STOP and report it as a finding rather than weakening the test.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: the cross-worktree test written and observed failing (absent-before assertion proves the store is not shared by directory) — manual attest
postconditions.satisfied_by: RED observed for real: first run FAILED on the raw byte-identity assertion across worktrees (b'...\n' != b'...\r\n'). Root cause is not a test bug — system core.autocrlf=true converts on checkout, so an episode's WORKING-TREE bytes are not worktree-stable on Windows. Corrected the claim to what is actually true (record equal, git blob hash equal, bytes equal modulo line endings) and pinned the hazard as its own named test rather than tuning it away.

postconditions.statement: green: seeded+committed in worktree W, retrieved from worktree R after the ordinary git path; `git worktree list` shows two real linked worktrees

constraints: a real git worktree add, never a directory-name simulation

m7-c4-nonforeclosure.title: C4 — dispute one agent-supplied field; sibling byte-identical
m7-c4-nonforeclosure.imperative: Seed an episode, capture the raw BYTES of the file, apply a dispute (amend-assertion) to exactly ONE agent-supplied assertion, then prove BY RETRIEVAL that (a) the disputed field's lifecycle-standing changed, (b) a sibling agent-supplied field's standing is unchanged, and (c) the sibling's stored line/block is BYTE-IDENTICAL before and after. Read with open(path,'rb') so no \r\n translation can mask or fake the byte comparison; state the newline choice.

postconditions.statement: TDD red: the non-foreclosure retrieval test written and observed failing — manual attest
postconditions.satisfied_by: No honest RED: the dispute write path is g2's and was already green; the retrieval side was green at m2. Falsified instead by construction — the byte comparison slices the sibling block out of the RAW bytes (open/read_bytes, no decoding, no newline translation), and the final assertion proves the only bytes that changed anywhere in the file are a4's, so a rewrite of any sibling would fail it.

postconditions.statement: green: disputed standing changed, sibling standing unchanged, sibling block byte-identical

constraints: byte comparison over raw bytes, not decoded text
